newsitem.title: USA: USDA seeks comments on meat recovery systems.
newsitem.headline: USDA seeks comments on meat recovery systems.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department on Thursday called for public comments on how to enforce its new regulations on meat and bone separation machinery.

"Because of concerns ... raised by consumer groups and industry in meetings and correspondence, FSIS decided to publish a notice requesting comments on the methods of enforcing compliance with the regulation," Food Safety and Inspection Service administrator Thomas Billy said.
Among other concerns, consumer groups have said that residue left by meat recovery processes could increase the risk of transmitting diseases.
The notice will be published in the November 8 Federal Register, and will call for public comment by January 8, USDA said.

In December 1994, USDA published a rule saying that meat produced by high-tech meat recovery systems is comparable in appearance, texture and composition to meat trimmings and similar products, and can fairly be described as "meat."
